notes: The reading is decided as for 1985-GR-IX.4.5.4-18 (same words, same conflict with the 04 definition, here §1985:VIII.1.3.4): B, latitude, and PB5238's retirement stands on the reading. Own probe relsep (RECORD VARYING 4 TO 30 over one 12-character description, records of 6, 30 and 12) reads 00/00/00, which B requires and A would make 04/04/00. The held probe is the other half and it overturns the CONFORMS under B as well: c4c.cob opens RDF (RECORD VARYING 5 TO 10) INPUT on a zero-byte file, a second connector writes a 3- and a 20-character record, and RDF's READs give 00 with LR 03 and LR 20, the second record truncated to the 10 characters of RDF's maximum; RDF's later OPEN gives 39, so the store's attributes do conflict with the reader's. Both records lie outside the reader's own record size (5 to 10) under either reading; GR16 makes such a READ successful with the record length conflict status, and the runtime even performs GR16's truncation while reporting 00. The read's premise (OPEN validation keeps every record inside the range, DOC-A.1-129) does not hold for a zero-byte store (StoreFormat.Empty validates nothing), and RelativeConnector's READs have no 04 arm. Secondary: after the truncating READ, LR is 20, above the reader's maximum of 10 and larger than the record the area holds; with 04 set and the record truncated "to the maximum size", the record just read (GR11) is the 10-character one; the fix should settle LR with the status. Under the under-OPEN (B) half, whether an OPEN INPUT of a zero-byte store should instead fix the attributes it will check is an implementor choice (GR8) the fix may make in place of the READ arm, but one of the two is required. PARTIAL, wrong-answer, silent. kb/Work PB5480 holds the defect (adjudication: held-85/set8/decisions.json (the adjudication of coderead-85/held-9.json, the 1985 read 4)).

The right-truncation and undefined-tail results are no longer stated for relative files.
